# REGISTER — mutation-proofs.wave7-capgr: # Companion to `mutation-proofs.tsv` (FROZEN) and to the other partial/wave registers. Scope: the
# guards added for `reference-impl/capability_grid.py`, which until this wave had NO TEST OF ANY
# KIND — nothing in the tree imported it, and its only check was `tools/regen_figures.py`'s
# PIXEL-EXACT diff of the committed PNG. That gate is unsound across machines: two GitHub Actions
# runs with identical numpy 2.4.6 / Pillow 12.3.0 / CPython 3.11.16 on ubuntu-latest produced
# different numbers (canyon+strata pit-storage 5.22e+06 vs 4.16e+06 m3; Monument Valley relief 259
# vs 268 m) and five figures drifted, `capability_grid` among them. With the pixel gate removed,
# 56 capabilities were left with nothing asserting anything about them at all.
# TWO DEFECTS WERE FIXED IN THE SUBJECT, both of the silent-fallthrough class this repo has already
# retired twice (`graph_demo._noise_fn`'s `else: perlin`, `_area_fn`):
#   1. `build` wrapped every tile's thunk in a bare `except Exception` and painted a dark-red "ERR"
#      swatch in its place, so a capability that had STOPPED WORKING still rendered a figure that
#      looked successful. The figure's own header is the claim being falsified: "every tile
#      generated live in pure numpy". The swatch path now exists only behind an explicit
#      `on_error="swatch"` opt-in and still reports every failure in the returned facts.
#   2. `build` returned None, so nothing downstream could assert anything. It now returns
#      `(canvas, facts)` the way `crater_anatomy.build` does, with per-tile status/shape/spread.
# A THIRD, adjudicated here: `_hero` read `hero.png` behind `except Exception: return gray(_terr)`,
# substituting a grey hillshade of a mountain for the imported 3D render under the caption
# "z-buffer, back-face cull, translucent water". Made LOUD. `tools/regen_figures.py:88-97` already
# records that this fallback made the tile "quietly draw SOMETHING ELSE" in a bare scratch
# directory, surfacing only as an unfixable 200x200 pixel drift and forcing READS_FIGURES plus a
# build-order rule as a workaround; loud turns that into a named missing input. A FOURTH, same
# class: `_norm` passed non-finite input straight through, and `(nan * 255).astype(np.uint8)` is 0,
# so a NaN-producing capability left as a uniformly BLACK tile that reads as a dark render.
# METHOD. Every mutation is applied to the SUBJECT (`capability_grid.py`), never to the test. Each
# trial: clear every `__pycache__` under reference-impl, sleep > 1 s (this repo has hit a false RED
# from CPython's .pyc cache when a byte-length-identical mutation was reverted inside one second),
# run `python -m pytest tests/test_capability_grid.py -q --tb=line`, paste the real failing test id
# and first failure line, revert from a pristine copy, and confirm with `diff` against that copy.
# Every row also carries a DECOY: a legitimate edit of similar shape the guard must NOT fire on.
# The guard module costs ~75 s because it runs all 56 live simulations ONCE at module scope and
# shares them; that pass is the reason every trial below reports 9 tests.
# Baseline for these runs: 9 passed in ~75 s.
